questions.stem: Why is graphite soft and slippery?

options.text: It has weak covalent bonds that break easily
It has weak intermolecular forces between its layers, allowing them to slide over each other
It has delocalised electrons that act as a lubricant
It has a simple molecular structure with small molecules

questions.explanation: Graphite has a layered structure with strong covalent bonds within each hexagonal layer, but only weak intermolecular forces between the layers. These weak forces allow the layers to slide over each other easily, making graphite soft and useful as a lubricant.

questions.stem: Silicon dioxide (SiO2) has a very high melting point of 1713 degrees C. What explains this?

options.text: It is a simple molecular substance with very strong intermolecular forces
It contains ionic bonds between silicon and oxygen ions
It has a giant covalent structure with many strong covalent bonds that must be broken
It has metallic bonding with delocalised electrons

questions.explanation: Silicon dioxide has a giant covalent structure similar to diamond. Each silicon atom is bonded to 4 oxygen atoms, and each oxygen is bonded to 2 silicon atoms, forming a continuous 3D network of strong covalent bonds. Many of these strong bonds must be broken to melt it, requiring a great deal of energy.
